newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.African rand/bonds closing report.
newsitem.headline: S.African rand/bonds closing report.

text.p: The rand firmed to its best level since August 7 as a rash of positive factors drove the rand more than two cents firmer on Friday.
At the local finish, the rand was quoted at 4.4845/4895 from 4.5080/5130 on Thursday after touching an intraday best level of 4.48 bid on the dollar.

The rand's gains came after a week in which July money supply and trade data bettered expectations. Several technical support levels for the dollar were also broken during the week, which squeezed out some long speculative positions.

Dealers said that on Friday, a large dollar sell order -- said by one dealer to be in the region of $100 million -- placed by diamond producer De Beers drove the unit through the psychological 4.50 barrier during the morning session.
"That triggered some orders out of Switzerland which pulled it back above 4.50 and then the weight of the diamond dollars pushed it lower again," a dealer said.
Dealers said that importers had largely kept to the sidelines on the day, indicating that that they were fairly well covered and implying that the currency could firm further next week.
"I think there is potentiat for the rand to strengthen to 4.35 and even 4.30," one trader said.
But another trader felt that the rand would have a tough time breaking the key 4.45 level.

"A lot of people have been talking about the 4.45 level as fair value, even the Reserve Bank," one dealer said. "I would think the the Bank will try and prop up its reserves and the losses on its forward book," the dealer said.

South Africa's gross gold and foreign exchange reserves stood at 10.37 billion rand in July -- a paltry 1.1 months import cover, while bank governor Chris Stals revealed earlier this week that the bank's net oversold foreign exchange position had grown to $15 billion from $8.1 billion at the end of February 1996.
Dealers said that the market would be wary of the release next Friday of August reserves data, which a Reuters consensus poll of economists forecast at 10.1 billion rand.
"But up until Friday the market will not have much to focus on and I expect the rand to range-trade between 4.47 and 4.51," a trader said.
Against the crosses, the rand was last at 7.0096/0210 on sterling from 7.0197/0320 on Thursday and at 0.3286/3295 marks from 0.3278/3284 marks previously.

Bond yields moved to their best levels since July 24 as the market took heart from the stronger rand and the positive economic indicators released earlier in the week, while shrugging off weakness on the U.S. Treasury bond market.
Dealers said that a number of technical levels had been broken throughout the week and the key R150 looked set to test the 15 percent barrier next week.
"I think the next big level will be the 15.03 level...beyond that 14.70," a dealer said.
The R150 was last quoted at 15.20 percent after touching an intraday best of 15.16 -- a six-week low -- from 15.30 percent on Thursday, while Eskom's 168 was at 15.35 percent from 15.46 percent.

Bond Exchange figures showed foreigners were net sellers of 8.42 million rand of South African bonds on Thursday after selling 98.42 million rand on Wednesday. Nominal cumulative volumes were pegged at 43.91 billion rand on Thursday -- a settlement day -- from 6.87 billion rand on Wednesday.

On the money market, three-month NCDs were lower at between 16.05 to 16.20 percent from 16.50 and 16.65 percent on Thursday, while 90-day BAs were lower at between 15.50 and 15.70 percent from 15.90 and 16.05 percent previously.
The Reserve Bank said the money market shortage surged to 9.208 billion rand on Wednesday from 8.705 billion rand on Tuesday. Latest figures were not immediately unavailable.
-- Paul Richardson, Johannesburg newsroom, +27 11 482-1003
